children: Japan's Ministry of Finance said on Thursday that any increase in defence spending should not be financed through new government bond issuances, as the government prepares to revise its strategy and spending plans for the next five years.
The ministry made the call at a meeting of the Fiscal System Council, an advisory panel on fiscal policy, a ministry official said.

The government is weighing a 70 trillion yen to 80 trillion yen ($443 billion to $507 billion) defence buildup plan for the fiscal years 2027 to 2031, nearly double the current five-year programme of about 43 trillion yen, sources have said.
Japan has been under pressure from the US to raise its defence spending to 3.5% of gross domestic product, which Washington has said should be a global standard for its allies.
Japan has yet to decide on any specific means of funding a potential increase in defence spending, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said last month.
Local media outlets have reported that an additional corporate tax increase has emerged within the government as a possible source of funding for a planned defence budget expansion.
